checks: Read s353 (likelihood, hypotheses) and out/q57/s353/s354_1.6-2.0.txt; the numbers in the report (Delta chi2 7.7/5.0/3.2/3.7, BF 1.25/0.59/0.64/51, A_N/A_S 1.26-2.5, contrast 1.09/1.23 etc.) match the output files. Agree with the logic: Hexc/Hcol best fits give 1.09-1.13 (1-0), 1.23-1.35 (3-2) vs 1.45/1.50.

Likelihood is linear-Gaussian with per-line sigma^2 = stat^2 + (5% I_obs)^2 + (10% I_mod)^2 and a shared 3-2 band scale (+-10%). A contrast built from 4 lines then carries ~20% error, so a model 1.2 vs obs 1.45 is ~1-1.5 sigma, not obviously 2.5-3 sigma. The Delta chi2 values include sigma-normalisation terms and are not for equal dof: Hcol vs Hfull is ~1-2 extra parameters (Delta chi2 5 = ~2.2 sigma), Hexc ~3 (7.7 = ~2 sigma). The '2.5-3 sigma-equivalent' wording over-claims; the Bayes factors (0.3-1.25) say no preference. Please state it as ~2 sigma at most and let BF carry the conclusion.

Physical consistency check (done by hand): the best-fit solutions sit at the grid edge log n=3.0 with N(HCO+)=2e16 (N) and Tk 190-300 K. With [HCO+]/[H2] 1e-9-1e-8 this implies N(H2)=2e24-2e25 and a path length N/n = 0.6-6 kpc, versus a 2.2" beam of ~0.4 kpc (and a ~100 pc core at N). The low-n/high-Tk/eta~0.1 branch, which dominates every hypothesis and the A_N/A_S posterior, is therefore not physical. Posteriors, BFs and the excitation-only limit are all computed over it. Not checked by the worker.

Habun has BF 51 vs Hfull (16 for X 20-200), i.e. ~40 vs Hexc, and the 'pure abundance' fit has Delta chi2 3.7 with far fewer parameters than Hexc/Hcol. The work summary omits this and says only 'not excluded by evidence'. The report entry lists 51 but the conclusion does not discuss that the Occam-dominated comparison actually favours abundance-only (same Tk,n,N,X) over excitation-only by a large factor; this must be stated together with its prior dependence.

All models over-predict S H13CN (0.7-0.9 vs 0.24+-0.35, and the N H13CN/H13CO+ fit is also off by 20-30%); X_S ~100 hits the prior edge. The S 13C constraint is what drives A_N/A_S and the HcolX substitute, and it is a ~1.5 sigma tension. Fine to keep, but the headline must say the A_N/A_S result relies on S H13CN being low.

Consistency with the team's earlier statements: Q29/Q34/Q44 gave A_N 3.6-5, A_S 2.0-2.5, tau(HCO+) 1.5 at N, n 1e4, Tk 22-112 K at N; Q57 now finds n=1e3, Tk>100 at N. The two Q57 solutions differ from the earlier ones by 1-2 dex in n and 3-10x in Tk; this is not reconciled in the report.

fixes.what: Add a physical prior/constraint to the RADEX grid and rerun all hypotheses: log n >= 4 (or extend the grid below 3 and show the best fit is not at the edge), and a path-length condition L = N(HCO+)/([HCO+]/[H2] n) <= ~beam (200-450 pc; N core ~100 pc) with [HCO+]/[H2] 1e-9-1e-8, or equivalently N(H2) from the dust/CO of the team. Report Delta chi2, BF, A_N/A_S and the maximum contrast reachable by excitation/opacity-only with and without it.
fixes.why: The currently winning solutions are kpc-long, n=1e3 columns at the grid edge; every number in the entry (including the 'excitation-only cannot reach 1.45' bound and A_N/A_S) is conditioned on them. Restricting to physical solutions probably reduces the reachable excitation contrast further or shifts Tk/n to the Q34 values.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Radex/LVG fits of dense-gas tracers always bound the column by n*L with an abundance prior (or fit N(H2) from dust), report the best fit not at the prior edge, and use a filling factor linked to the same geometry.

fixes.what: Recalibrate the significance language: convert Delta chi2 to p-values with the actual dof (Hexc~3, Hcol~1-2, Habun~?), propagate the contrast uncertainty (e.g. +-0.10 from Q56 plus the 10% model term) and give the max excitation-only contrast with a confidence band (profile likelihood on the contrast), instead of '2.5-3 sigma'.
fixes.why: Delta chi2 5-7.7 with 1-3 dof is ~2 sigma and the BF is ~1; the entry says both 'under-produce at 2.5-3 sigma' and 'not excluded' without reconciling them.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Profile the likelihood in the derived quantity (N/S contrast) per hypothesis and quote the contrast at which Delta chi2=1,4.

fixes.what: Discuss Habun vs Hexc/Hcol explicitly (BF 16-51 vs ~1) and test the Occam sensitivity: rerun with the 10% model-error and 5% systematics halved/doubled and with an alternative prior on log n (flat in log n over 3-6), reporting how BF(Habun)/BF(Hexc) moves.
fixes.why: This is the most informative evidence for the question and is currently missing from the conclusions.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Quote the evidence ratio range under a set of reasonable priors and error models, as done in Q29.

fixes.what: Derive the physical consequence: HCN abundance enhancement at N given A_N/A_S and the 12C/13C scenario, and the alternative 'X_S>=130' scenario in terms of what it would require for the other isotopologue ratios (HN13C, 13CO if available), and reconcile with Q34/Q44 solutions (n, Tk).
fixes.why: The result is stated as a ratio of columns only; the 12C/13C substitution is flagged but its testable consequences are not derived.
fixes.how_experts_do_it: Predict the other 13C ratios under each branch, so that the next dataset can discriminate.
